SHORT_DESCRIPTION: FEASIBILITY STUDY - IBHUBESI OFFSHORE GAS SUBSURFACE FIELD DEVELOPMENT FEASIBILITY STUDY, THROUGH MHA PETROLEUM CONSULTANTS LLC
PROJECT_TITLE: Feasibility Study - Ibhubesi Offshore Gas Subsurface Field Development Feasibility Study, through MHA Petroleum Consultants LLC
LONG_DESCRIPTION: This grant to Sunbird Energy Ltd (South Africa) is funding a Subsurface Field Development Plan for the Ibhubesi Offshore Gas Project. The Subsurface Field Development Plan will be integrated with a Full Field Development Plan being commissioned by Sunbird Energy to define the project engineering requirements and complete an environmental impact assessment and commercial analysis for the development of proven natural gas reserves located off the western coast of South Africa. The study is constructing a detailed 3D gas reservoir model, assessing production flow rates, identifying preferred drilling locations, and completing a well design to maximize production against cost and integration with the facilities development plan. If implemented, the introduction of natural gas from Ibhubesi would help to alleviate South Africa's energy shortage, increase diversity and security of the energy supply, and mitigate carbon emissions by displacing current diesel and coal power generation in the Western Cape Province. The study is being completed by MHA Petroleum Consultants LLC.

The project would be expected to result in the construction of a 100 MW CSP plant, and would be expected to support human capacity building through the creation of low-, medium-, and highly skilled jobs as well as provide significant positive environmental impacts and climate change mitigation through the reduction of carbon dioxide emission generation.

SHORT_DESCRIPTION: FEASIBILITY STUDY - MEERKAT 18 MEGAWATT SMALL HYDROPOWER PROJECT FEASIBILITY STUDY, THROUGH AECOM TECHNOLOGY CORPORATION

LONG_DESCRIPTION: A USTDA grant to Meerkat Hydropower (Pty) Ltd is funding a feasibility study (FS) that is evaluating the technical, financial, and other aspects of the 18-40 megawatt (MW) Run-of-the-River Hydropower Plant in South Africa's Northern Cape Province. If implemented, the hydropower plant would add 18-40 MW of generation capacity, thereby helping to diversify South Africa's energy mix and reduce environmental emissions associated with fossil fuel power sources. Meerkat Hydropower intends to submit a bid for the Meerkat plants in the fifth round of South Africa's Renewable Energy Independent Power Producer Procurement Program. This activity is eligible for financing under the U.S. - Africa Clean Energy Finance Initiative.

SHORT_DESCRIPTION: FEASIBILITY STUDY - URBAN SOLAR FARMS FEASIBILITY STUDY, THROUGH MOTT MACDONALD GROUP LTD.
PROJECT_TITLE: Feasibility Study - Urban Solar Farms Feasibility Study, through Mott MacDonald Group Ltd.
LONG_DESCRIPTION: This USTDA grant to SolarReserve South Africa (Proprietary) Limited is funding a feasibility study to assess the technical, financial and economic viability of, and develop a blueprint for, an initial 50 MW and ultimately approximately 200 MW of solar photovoltaic sub-projects in urban areas in South Africa, with most of the sub-projects ranging in size from 5 MW to 30 MW. These sub-projects would intend to provide power to residential, commercial and industrial end users directly or through a wheeling arrangement with municipal distribution companies.

LONG_DESCRIPTION: The installation of photovoltaics in Upper Blinkwater provides practical insights into feasibility and necessary framework conditions for a sustainable, decentralized energy supply. The project will install BettaFour solar light kits in the homes of community members, altogether 130 households in Kwadlakuse and Esikhuthwaneni, two deeply rural villages in Northern KwaZulu-Natal, which is one of the poorest regions in South Africa largely due to its history as a marginalised homeland. Access to electricity is important for the rural poor as it reduces especially women's work burden, improve people's standards of living and children's educational outcomes. Earlier the households have met their energy needs using fossil fuels and/or biomass. Project will contribute to climate change mitigation, as fossil fuels will be replaced by solar power. Project's solar kits were selected as they offer a practical and cost effective way to provide light to rural households living in isolated areas. The system consists of four 1 watt LED lights, a controller with lead crystal battery, a 10 watt solar panel and a 10Ah 6 Volt Lead crystal battery. Solar power provides communities lightning without costs.The installation will involve members from each household and basic training on the use of the unit will be provided to promote long term sustainability. Each household will also be required to sign a social contract which explains that (unless defective) the property becomes their responsibility. In addition to overseeing the installation of the lighting kits, ACT mentors will provide assistance in the development of homestead food gardens, as well as offer advice in ways to store and save water when they visit the households. The proposed project will be four months in duration and budget is inclusive of all equipment, administration costs and tax. Monitoring will take place throughout the project and periodic visits will also be conducted by ACT teams once the project has been completed.
